text: You're typing a quick message, perfectly normal, when your phone's predictive text suggests something utterly bizarre. It's baffling, isn't it?
You just want to type efficiently, but these bizarre suggestions interrupt your flow. It feels like the phone should know *you* better.
You might think it’s poorly designed, or picking up strange habits from *your* typing. You correct it, but the weirdness persists.
The truth is, your phone’s brain isn’t just your typing history. It's a massive algorithm trained on billions of words from the entire internet – articles, conversations, every text imaginable.
This giant dataset includes all the internet’s quirks and biases. So, while it guesses common phrases, it also learns obscure, nonsensical connections.
So next time your phone suggests 'flibbertigibbet' instead of 'finish', you'll know it's not broken. It's reflecting the wild, vast world of text it was trained on.
